cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet in Judah, has just heard the LORD announce disaster coming on Jerusalem (Jeremiah 15:1-9). Now he cries out about his own life: "Woe to me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife and conflict in all the land." Friend, most of us complain about Mondays, and Jeremiah's complaining about the day he was BORN.

cards.question: Jeremiah says everyone curses him over money he lent or borrowed.

cards.text: When I complained in that junk drawer, the only ones who answered were the dead batteries I shared it with, and they were LYING about how much charge they had left. Jeremiah cries out, and the LORD Himself speaks: He will surely deliver Jeremiah for a good purpose.

cards.question: The LORD says that in the time of trouble and distress, He will intercede with the enemy.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks the kind of question you don't answer out loud, like Mother Miller asking who stole the cookie dough while the spoon's still in your hand. Can anyone smash iron, iron from the north, or bronze?

cards.question: The LORD asks if anyone can smash iron from the north, or bronze. What answer is that question pointing to?

answers.text: Only a king can smash it
Anyone with fire can smash it

cards.text: Then the LORD's words turn: wealth and treasures given up as plunder, without charge. That's a FREE giveaway, friend, and nobody's lining up for this one.

cards.question: The LORD says the wealth and treasures will be given up as plunder for all your ___.
Next the LORD says His anger will kindle a fire, and "you" will be enslaved to the enemies. Where?

answers.text: In a land you do not know
In a land you have seen before
In the land your fathers knew

cards.text: Now Jeremiah turns back to God, and he doesn't hold back: "You understand, O LORD; remember me and attend to me."

cards.question: Jeremiah asks the LORD to do something about his persecutors. What is it?

cards.text: In one breath he wants payback, and in the next he asks the LORD, in His patience, not to take him away. That was me every time the junk drawer opened: "Somebody DO something!" and also "PLEASE don't clean this drawer out!"

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD he endures reproach for his own honor.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah talks about the LORD's words. "Your words were found," he says, and he treats them the way the Millers treated a fresh batch of my cookies.

cards.question: When the LORD's words were found, what does Jeremiah say he did with them?
Jeremiah says the LORD's words became a heavy burden he could hardly carry.

cards.text: Not a burden. The LORD's words became his JOY and his heart's delight. Friend, the Millers stole cookie dough off my counter for YEARS, and not once did anybody eat the RECIPE and call it their favorite part.
Then Jeremiah tells the LORD, "For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts." And he says he never sat with the band of revelers, and he never celebrated with them.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD that because the LORD's hand was on him, he sat ___.

cards.text: The revelers are celebrating, and Jeremiah's sitting alone, and friend, I KNOW that seat, because I had the back-of-the-junk-drawer version for years. Then he adds, "for You have filled me with indignation."
Jeremiah asks why his pain is unending and his wound won't heal. Then he tells the LORD what He has become like to him.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD has become like what to him?

cards.text: A mirage. Water that isn't there. Friend, I wouldn't say that to my BOSS'S face, and Jeremiah's saying it straight to GOD.
So the LORD answers him. I'd have braced myself for a lecture, but His answer starts with one small word: if.

cards.question: The LORD says that if Jeremiah returns, He will restore him, and Jeremiah will stand in His presence.

cards.text: Then comes a second if, about what comes out of Jeremiah's mouth: if he speaks words that are noble instead of worthless. That's the rule every group chat on earth NEEDS pinned to the top.

cards.question: If Jeremiah speaks noble words instead of worthless ones, what does the LORD say he will be?
The LORD tells Jeremiah that the people must turn to him, but he must not turn to them.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Jeremiah what He will make him to this people. A wall.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make Jeremiah a fortified wall of ___ to this people.
The LORD says the people won't even try to fight against Jeremiah.
The people will fight against Jeremiah, but the LORD says they won't overcome him. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD is with him to save him
The people are too afraid of him
The king's guards will protect him

cards.text: And the LORD's not done promising. He has one more line for Jeremiah, about the wicked and the ruthless.

cards.question: In His last line, what does the LORD promise to do for Jeremiah against the wicked and the ruthless?
